etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French oposite, from Latin oppositus, perfect passive participle of oppōnō (“I oppose”). Compare oppose.

definitions.definition: Located directly across from something else, or from each other.
(botany) Of leaves and flowers, positioned directly across from each other on a stem.
Of either of two complementary or mutually exclusive things.
Extremely different; inconsistent; contrary; repugnant; antagonistic.

quote.citation: 1697, Virgil, “Dedication”, in John Dryden, transl., The Works of Virgil: Containing His Pastorals, Georgics, and Æneis. […], London:  […]  Jacob Tonson, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Novels, by which the reader is misled into another sort of pieasure opposite to that which is designed in an epick poem.
Particles of speech have divers, and sometimes almost opposite, significations.

definitions.definition: Something opposite or contrary to something else.
A person or thing that is entirely different from or the reverse of someone or something else; used to show contrast between two people or two things.

quote.citation: 1906, Stanley J[ohn] Weyman, chapter I, in Chippinge Borough, New York, N.Y.: McClure, Phillips & Co., →OCLC, page 01:
quote.text: It was April 22, 1831, and a young man was walking down Whitehall in the direction of Parliament Street. […]. He halted opposite the Privy Gardens, and, with his face turned skywards, listened until the sound of the Tower guns smote again on the ear and dispelled his doubts.

definitions.definition: (television) On another channel at the same time.
